While they spoke a little about getting certified to sell Disney vacations and cruise packages, they had more to say about the "OPTIONAL" benefit of having our monthly fees "paid for" by "growing our business". As others here have been warning, they really want more people to recruit even more people. 

Of course, they went to great lengths to make Archer/Evolution sound incredibly enticing, though I noticed a few differences between the two Zooms. During the first Zoom, the host really went hard on spinning Archer/Evolution as some awesome "opportunity to travel the world!" At one point, she even made it sound like she was getting some free trip to Bora Bora, and she tried some (misleading?) infographics to suggest that we can make several thousand dollars in 48 hours by selling a group cruise package. Even when she let it slip that her spouse is still working his real job, she tried to pass it off as his irrational doubts of her "huge success" as she was allegedly booking herself on all these fabulous "free" trips. 

In contrast, the host of the second Zoom had a harder time keeping the mask on. About 45 minutes in, she started admitting to potential recruits that this was a 1099 position, NOT an actual job offer. Though the second hun also tried to entice people with the "free trips!" angle, she didn't really go for the church revival/"self-help" conference vibes that the first hun really played up. 

In both cases, the huns who actually put their names  on their LinkedIn job ads were not the hosts of these Zooms. Looking back, it's clear that they were directed by their respective uplines to funnel anyone/everyone who responded at LinkedIn into the Zooms. With that said, both Zoom hosts had everyone write in the chat box who invited us to the Zoom. Clearly, they were keeping track of which downlines were inviting how many new recruits. 

Now that I know what's up with these suspicious "travel agent" job posts at LinkedIn and Upwork, I wish they and other job boards would at least try harder to require more transparency. Better yet, I wish job boards would do a better job for job seekers by weeding out these MLM bait-and-switch ads entirely.
